definition: Semantic analytics, also termed semantic relatedness, is the use of ontologies to analyze content in web resources.
details: This field of research combines text analytics and Semantic Web technologies like RDF. Semantic analytics measures the relatedness of different ontological concepts. Some academic research groups that have active project in this area include Kno.e.sis Center at Wright State University among others.

explainer.lead: Semantic analytics, also called semantic relatedness, uses ontologies to analyze content in web resources. It combines text analytics with Semantic Web technologies like RDF and measures how related different ontological concepts are.

tiers.eli5: Like using an organized map of categories to see how closely two ideas on a website are connected.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers analyze web content against ontologies, using RDF-based Semantic Web technologies, and measure relatedness between concepts. The approach depends on the quality and coverage of the ontology used.
tiers.paperLevel: It is the use of ontologies to analyze content in web resources, combining text analytics and Semantic Web technologies such as RDF, and it measures the relatedness of different ontological concepts. Results are bounded by the ontology that defines the concepts.

explainer.example: A web resource's content is analyzed against an ontology, and the relatedness of two concepts in it is measured.
